artists.biography:
One of New York’s most notable ska bands, the Slackers formed in Brooklyn in 1991 and have played the world over many times since. Their first release was an eponymous self-released album, distributed by Moon Records in 1993 on cassette. Their first real debut is “Better Late Than Never” on moon ska records. Coming out in 1996, this album saw a movement to more traditional ska music, as opposed to their earlier two-tone and garage influences. It was produced by Victor Rice, a noted ska/reggae producer, who also played bass for them at one point.

Band members are as follows:
Vic Ruggiero - Keyboards, Vocals
Jay “Agent Jay” Nugent - Guitar
Dave Hillyard - Saxophone
Glen Pine - Trombone, Vocals
Marcus Geard - Bass
Ara Babajian - Drums

perplexity.description:
The Question is the third studio album by The Slackers, released in 1998 on Pirates Press Records. Following the commercial breakthrough of their previous album Redlight, the record represents a pivotal moment in the band's early career, arriving during an extraordinarily prolific period in which they released three albums within three years. The album showcases the band's fusion of rock, reggae, and ska influences, establishing their signature sound that blends Caribbean rhythms with punk-influenced energy and rock instrumentation.

The album's significance within The Slackers' catalog lies in its position as a consolidation of their emerging style during their most creatively active period. The Question has since been recognized as one of the band's early classic albums, demonstrating their ability to sustain artistic momentum following their breakthrough success. The record's enduring appeal is evidenced by its multiple reissues and remastered editions, including a 25th anniversary reissue released in 2023 that introduced the album to new audiences and solidified its status within the band's legacy.
